hypothesis: The simulation timeout and repeated retire PC/instruction mismatches are caused by the forwarding unit failing to supply EX-stage operands from the two valid forwarding paths (EX/MEM and MEM/WB). As a result, a branch/JALR in EX that depends on a register produced by an immediately preceding ALU instruction reads the stale register-file value instead of the forwarded result. The branch consequently resolves in the wrong direction or computes a wrong JALR target, redirecting the front-end to a wrong program path. Wrong-path instructions then retire and the expected ECALL/halt never occurs, producing the t13_dft mismatches until the 20 s timeout.
constraints: Do not change the forwarding_unit port names or bit widths.
Implement both EX/MEM -> EX and MEM/WB -> EX forwarding paths.
EX/MEM forwarding must have priority over MEM/WB when both match the same source register.
Never assert forwarding to x0 when the destination register is x0 or when the source register field is x0.
Do not forward from invalid pipeline stages; forward only when the corresponding valid and reg_write signals are true.
Do not alter pipeline stage boundaries, stall, flush, or reset semantics.
verification_targets: simulation_timeout must clear and the RTL must halt via ECALL with halted=1.
No t13_dft retire PC/instruction mismatch messages should appear.
A dependent branch/JALR immediately following an ALU instruction must resolve using the forwarded value, not the stale register-file value.
The expected 132 retired instructions and 64 control-transfer resolutions should complete without extra wrong-path retire events.
rejected_hypotheses: Icarus-unsupported packed-struct/array constructs in branch_predictor and dcache were the root cause.
Missing flush of younger pipeline stages after misprediction was the root cause.
Incomplete JALR target-change comparison in EX was the root cause.
WB retire_valid being a level instead of a one-cycle pulse was the root cause.
IF stage using pred_pc without gating on pred_pc_valid was the root cause.
